title: Zero pullback forces vanishing near the image
statement: Let R and T be schemes [def-pc-scheme], t:T -> R a morphism, G an abelian sheaf on the small etale site of R [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves], U an R-etale object and V a T-etale object [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], and phi:V -> U a morphism over t. If the pullback of g in G(U) to t^*G(V) along phi is zero [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image], then the image of phi is contained in the vanishing locus of g, defined as the union of images of etale arrows into U on which g restricts to zero.

mathlib_searches.query: The image of a morphism is contained in the vanishing locus of a section if the pullback section is zero

proof.text: At a point x of V use the proved library theorem exists_of_pullSection_eq_zero. Here is its argument: inverse image is sheafification of the presheaf left Kan extension. The equalizer sieve for the sheafification map is covering, so an etale neighbourhood a:Vprime -> V containing x detects equality with zero in that presheaf. The Kan extension is a filtered colimit along etale base change; eventual detection of zero supplies an etale b:Uprime -> U and phiPrime:Vprime -> Uprime with phiPrime followed by b = a followed by phi, and b^*g=0. This is the local-zero characterization of inverse image.

Choose xprime over x. Then phi(x)=b(phiPrime(xprime)); since the restriction of g along b is zero, phi(x) is in vanishingLocus by definition. This includes empty V. These are exactly the steps of the already proved source declaration range_subset_vanishingLocus_of_pullSection_eq_zero; no Lean declaration or sorry is added for this node.

lean.statement: lemma range_subset_vanishingLocus_of_pullSection_eq_zero {R T : Scheme.{u}} (t : T ⟶ R) (G : Sheaf R.smallEtaleTopology AddCommGrpCat.{u + 1}) {V : T.Etale} {U : R.Etale} (φ : V.left ⟶ U.left) (hφ : φ ≫ U.hom = V.hom ≫ t) (g : G.obj.obj (Opposite.op U)) (h : pullSection t G φ hφ g = 0) : Set.range φ ⊆ vanishingLocus G g
